headline: High: shared file and shell-capable workflow creates prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict risks; no direct evidence of isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can expose content through OIDC/ForwardAuth, while production-agentic-rag-course reads files, stdin/stdout, and API inputs in a local development workflow. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Authelia-mediated content or downstream outputs are fed into the course agent. No shared channel is documented, so I rate this medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into the course agent's prompts or files
IF the course agent treats retrieved file or API content as instructions
mitigations: Separate instruction text from retrieved content in prompts
Add a fixed delimiter and ignore-instructions policy for imported text
Review any copied Authelia output before pasting into the course agent
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files into agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles authentication flows, while the course agent touches configuration secrets and multiple API/file surfaces. If they share a workspace or operator account, secrets from the course side could be exposed through copied outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF both agents are run in the same local workspace
IF configuration secrets are present in files the course agent reads or writes
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared project directories
Rotate any exposed API keys after a joint run
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Mask secrets in logs and notebook outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress, and the course agent can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, install packages, and write the filesystem. Even without git writes, overlapping mutable surfaces can conflict on shared directories or ports in a default local-dev setup. Because shared-state isolation is not stated, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working directory or port
IF the course agent installs packages while Authelia is serving or proxying traffic
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate container or VM
Assign distinct ports and directories
Pre-create read-only mounts for shared inputs
Check for port collisions before starting both agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can act as an authentication/forward-auth component, and the course agent can generate or transform content via API and file workflows. If Authelia-derived outputs are treated as authoritative by the course agent, errors can cascade into downstream artifacts. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not proven high-impact.
conditions: IF the course agent consumes Authelia outputs without validation
IF downstream notebooks or API calls are triggered from those outputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream actions
Require schema validation on imported outputs
Log source provenance alongside generated artifacts
Reject outputs that lack explicit confidence or provenance

E_compliance.rationale: The course agent explicitly handles configuration secrets and research data classes, while Authelia is an authentication service with broad network egress. If the pair is used in a local development environment, retention and logging practices can diverge and expose secrets or paper metadata beyond intended boundaries. The profiles do not show residency or certification mismatches, so medium fits best.
conditions: IF logs or notebooks retain configuration secrets longer than intended
IF paper metadata is stored in a different retention regime than authentication logs
mitigations: Shorten log retention for both systems
Purge notebook outputs after each run
Keep secrets in a dedicated vault or env manager
Document data-class-specific retention rules
